solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Current parliament returns early work

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: returns tells us the parliament's name is read backwards, from its end to its start

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament

explanation.surface: A sitting parliament sends back an author's early piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dail is Ireland's lower house; 'returns' is the reversal signal, and 'early work' fits Homer's poem as one of the oldest in Western literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem is among the earliest surviving works of Western literature.

clue.text: Obscure country's losing a contest finally in court

indicators.note: losing means the country's word drops the letter a

parts.note: India's, the possessive of the country

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of contest

explanation.surface: A shadowy nation drops a case after it goes to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing a' takes one A out of INDIA'S to give INDIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscure is unclear or blurred, not sharply seen or heard.

clue.text: This author's taking in singular theory

indicators.note: taking in means the author's word swallows the singular letter

parts.note: the writer refers to themselves: this author is = I'm
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A writer admits to holding one particular theory.
explanation.walkthrough: I(S)M.
explanation.definitionFit: An ism is any doctrine or belief system, a word taken from suffixes like socialism.

clue.text: Current producer withdraws a good deal in style

indicators.note: in places the reversed word inside the style word

parts.note: a do is a hairdo, a hairstyle

indicators.note: withdraws means draws back, so the a-good-deal word runs backwards

parts.note: many means a great number, a good deal

explanation.surface: A power company pulls out of a lucrative deal with some panache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current producer' looks like a power company but is a generator; 'withdraws' is the reversal signal, and 'style' is a hairdo.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a generator that turns mechanical energy into electricity.

clue.text: Disastrously dropped litre drinks in school

indicators.note: in places the litre and drinks inside the word for school, which wraps around them

parts.note: a coed is a co-educational school, taking both boys and girls
laps means drinks as a cat does, with the tongue

explanation.surface: Someone drank too much at school and fell over badly.
explanation.walkthrough: CO + L LAPS + ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall down suddenly in a heap, as a building or a fainting person does, is a disastrous drop.

clue.text: In place of holiday, English cleaner in criminal court!

indicators.note: in puts the English cleaner inside the rearranged court
criminal means wrong or bad, so the letters of court are rearranged

parts.note: Daz is a British brand of washing powder

explanation.surface: Instead of a holiday, an English cleaner ends up in the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' is the anagram signal on 'court'; Daz is a British washing powder. 'In' before 'place of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The French Riviera, the Mediterranean coast around Nice and Cannes, is a famous holiday destination.

clue.text: Some delightfully rich little poem

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A short poem that is wonderfully rich in parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A short poem expressing personal feeling, originally sung to a lyre, is this kind of verse.

clue.text: Take a look into a large juvenile compound

indicators.note: into puts the a-look pair inside the juvenile word

parts.note: a kid is a child, a juvenile
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Peek at a big young chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: A L + K(A LO)ID; 'Take' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Alkaloids are nitrogen-containing organic substances such as caffeine, morphine and nicotine, a class of chemical compound.

clue.text: Three views about to be one

indicators.note: about means around, so the three viewing words surround to

parts.note: see, eye and eye are three words for view or look at

explanation.surface: Three different perspectives are on the point of converging.
explanation.walkthrough: SEE EYE (TO) EYE.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree fully is to be of one mind, to be united in opinion.

clue.text: Fool jolly officer

parts.note: a jolly is a party or outing, as is a do
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: A silly but cheerful officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' is the noun for a festive outing, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolt is a stupid person, a dunce or idiot.

clue.text: Master divisor, ignoring two quarters

indicators.note: ignoring says the two compass letters are left out of the divisor word

parts.note: the denominator of a fraction is the number it is divided by
E and N, east and north, are two of the four compass points or quarters

explanation.surface: A division sum where the expert skips over two parts of the fraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' drops the E and N that sit together near the front of DENOMINATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: One who dominates is a ruler or controller, someone with mastery over others.

clue.text: Armstrong's heard of what prayers do

indicators.note: heard says we want a word that is pronounced the same as the astronaut's first name

parts.note: Neil Armstrong, the first man to walk on the Moon

explanation.surface: A question about what the Moon-walking astronaut was overheard saying.
explanation.walkthrough: The K of the answer is silent, so it is pronounced exactly like the name Neil. 'Armstrong's' reads as 'Armstrong is'.
explanation.definitionFit: People at prayer traditionally go down on bended knee in church.

clue.text: Resorts employing treatment, having nothing for drug at intervals

parts.note: spas are health resorts

indicators.note: for signals a swap: the letter for nothing stands in place of the drug letter

parts.note: medically means by means of medical treatment
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
O, the round figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Health resorts that use treatments, swapping drugs for nothing, only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having nothing for drug' turns MEDICALLY into MODICALLY; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Spasmodic activity comes in fits and starts, so it happens irregularly, only every now and then.

clue.text: Like grass family doctor brought in, it's negotiable

indicators.note: brought in means the family doctor pieces are put inside the other two words

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
rice is a cereal grass
kin are one's family
a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor called in by a family of grass lovers says everything is open to discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: AS (KIN GP) RICE.
explanation.definitionFit: The seller's stated figure for a house or car is usually open to bargaining.

clue.text: As was Molly Brown, tanning in bleak sun

indicators.note: tanning means giving a beating, so the letters are knocked about

explanation.surface: A woman sunbathing in weak, pale sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tanning' looks like sunbathing but means thrashing, hence the shuffle of IN BLEAK SUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Brown survived the Titanic disaster and was nicknamed by the musical 'The ___ Molly Brown'.

clue.text: Unpleasant, and very cold, outside King's Head

indicators.note: outside means the cold word goes round the outside of the king's letter

parts.note: icy means very cold

indicators.note: a head is the top or front, so the first letter of King is taken

explanation.surface: A shiver of distaste as an icy blast surrounds the head of the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: IC(K)Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Icky is informal for sticky and nasty, so something disagreeable or distasteful.

clue.text: Republic disperses beatniks pursuing sawn-off gun

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so the rearranged letters follow the shortened gun
sawn-off says the gun's word has its end cut short, as a shotgun barrel is sawn off

parts.note: the Uzi is an Israeli submachine gun

indicators.note: disperses says the letters of beatniks are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Bohemian beatniks scatter while being chased by someone with a cut-down shotgun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sawn-off' trims the gun's last letter and 'disperses' is the anagram signal; 'pursuing' puts the shuffled part second.
explanation.definitionFit: This former Soviet state in Central Asia is a republic with Tashkent as its capital.

clue.text: Try nut and bolt to secure area

parts.note: in printing an en is called a nut, from 'en quad'

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so the bolt word encloses the area letter

parts.note: to bolt food is to devour it

explanation.surface: Fixing something with nut and bolt to make an area safe.
explanation.walkthrough: EN + DE(A)VOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: An endeavour is an attempt or effort, a try.

clue.text: Skirt round old temple displaying measure of power

indicators.note: round means the skirt word goes around the old temple

parts.note: a kilt is a Scottish pleated skirt
a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia

explanation.surface: A kilt wrapped around an ancient temple to show off its might.
explanation.walkthrough: KIL(O WAT)T.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of electrical power equal to a thousand watts.

clue.text: Give up introducing complex rating scale

indicators.note: introducing means the give-up word takes the jumbled letters into its middle

parts.note: to cede is to give up or surrender

indicators.note: complex means intricate or tangled, so the letters of rating are mixed up

explanation.surface: Abandoning a complicated rating system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' is the anagram signal on 'rating'; the result goes inside the word for give up. The scale is the old name for Celsius.
explanation.definitionFit: The Celsius temperature scale, with a hundred degrees between freezing and boiling water, was long called this.

clue.text: Still, one that's never been authenticated

definitions.note: the definition reads with 'one' as 'one that's never been authenticated', a creature never proved real

parts.note: yet means still, as in 'not done yet'
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Even now, here is one thing no one has ever verified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' does double duty in the surface: it gives I and also leads into the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Abominable Snowman of the Himalayas is a legendary creature whose existence has never been proved.

clue.text: Fighter once assembled eastern troops

parts.note: met means gathered or assembled
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A warrior of the past gathered his men from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gloster Meteor was a British jet fighter of the 1940s and 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gloster Meteor was Britain's first operational jet aircraft for air combat.

clue.text: Cruisers might lie along this front, playing cards

parts.note: a seafront is a promenade, the walkway along the shore
a deck is a pack of playing cards

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers relax on the seafront over a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cruisers' are people on a cruise, not warships.
explanation.definitionFit: An upper deck of a cruise liner where passengers stroll or lounge on deckchairs in the sun.

clue.text: Poles in Brussels start to examine result

indicators.note: in puts the poles inside the Brussels letters

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the EU, the European Union
N and S are the north and south poles

indicators.note: start to takes the first letter of examine

explanation.surface: Polish people in Brussels are about to inspect the outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: E(NS)U + E; 'Poles' is not people from Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow as a consequence, so to result, as a verb.

clue.text: Cut theatre for men only

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the theatre word loses its last letter

parts.note: the stage is the theatre as an art or profession

explanation.surface: A shortened theatre show for an all-male audience.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag night or stag party is a men-only celebration before a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag event, such as a stag party, is attended only by males.

clue.text: In which the beast of Siberia is caught?

definitions.text: In which the beast of Siberia is caught?

parts.words: In which the beast of Siberia is caught?
parts.note: the Siberian tiger lives in the northern snow forest, whose name, said in a non-rhotic accent, sounds like 'tiger'

explanation.surface: A question about where a Siberian animal is trapped.
explanation.walkthrough: The forest's name and 'tiger' sound alike, which 'caught' hints at by suggesting something heard as well as trapped.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger of Siberia roams the vast subarctic coniferous forest belt of northern Russia.

clue.text: Screen producer's turkey chasing small donkey

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the flop word comes after the small donkey

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
moke is an old British slang word for a donkey
a turkey is a flop, and in British slang a bomb is a flop too

explanation.surface: A film producer's flop trails behind a little donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen' is a smokescreen, not a cinema screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that releases a dense cloud to hide troops from the enemy produces a smokescreen.

clue.text: Away side at Old Trafford

definitions.meaning: Old Trafford in Manchester is a cricket ground as well as Manchester United's football stadium

explanation.surface: The visiting team at Manchester United's ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests football, but the side is the cricket term, off side.
explanation.definitionFit: Gone or absent is off, and in cricket the off side is one half of the field.

clue.text: Stars dealing with a disease hooked by drugs

indicators.note: hooked by means caught and held, so the drugs word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: gear is slang for illegal drugs
re means concerning or about
TB is tuberculosis

explanation.surface: Celebrities with an illness who are addicted to drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: G(RE A TB)EAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursa Major is the large northern constellation that contains the Plough, so it is a group of stars.

clue.text: Toy with no head found in sack

indicators.note: with no head means the toy word loses its first letter

parts.note: to trifle with something is to toy with it

explanation.surface: A headless toy discovered in a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sack' looks like a noun for a bag but is the verb, to plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack is to search and plunder, which is also what to sack a town means.
